payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His (BTK, UniProt Q06187) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_000061.3(BTK):c.83G>A (p.Arg28His) as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 8 submissions) for X-linked agammaglobulinemia.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: UniProtKB natural variant VAR_006220 at residue 28 (R to H) is annotated as moderate in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, with 6 publications cited.
UniProtKB annotates residue 28 of Q06187 as a binding site for 1D-myo-inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate, based on experimental evidence (PubMed 10196129).
UniProtKB annotates residues 3-133 of Q06187 as the PH domain, from computational sequence-model evidence.
AlphaMissense gives p.Arg28His of Q06187 a pathogenicity score of 0.9978, classed as likely pathogenic.
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.statement: ScoreCons gives residue 28 of Q06187 a conservation score of 0.962 on a 0 to 1 scale across UniRef90.

39 of 170 experimental PDB structures of Q06187 observe residue 28, and 35 of those carry the reference arginine; the residue is ligand-proximal across several entries, with zinc ions present in all 39 and inositol phosphate ligand 4IP in 1BWN and 1B55.
PDB 1B55 (2.4 Å X-ray) is a PH domain of BTK in complex with inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate (4IP) and zinc.
PDB 6TT2 (1.36 Å X-ray) is the BTK PH domain carrying the R28C mutation, with zinc and magnesium ions and no inositol phosphate ligand listed.
A 2013 molecular dynamics study simulated BTK PH domain wild type and mutants including R28C/H with Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 to examine changes in the ligand binding site.
UniProtKB subunit annotation says BTK binds GTF2I through its PH domain and interacts with IBTK via its PH domain, so the PH domain carries protein-binding contacts as well as lipid binding.
No experimental measurement was found of R28H stability, IP4 binding affinity, or membrane recruitment for the R28H substitution itself.
payload.why_it_matters: Without these, it is unclear whether R28H acts by losing lipid-head-group contact, by destabilising the PH fold, or by disrupting a protein interface.

payload.statement: ClinVar lists three pathogenic substitutions at residue 28 of BTK: R28H, R28C (VCV000946996.13) and R28L (VCV001075550.10, pathogenic/likely pathogenic), all with no conflicts.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: A 1996 EMBO Journal study reports distinct phosphoinositide specificity of the pleckstrin homology domains of dynamin and Bruton's tyrosine kinase, establishing BTK PH domain as a phosphoinositide binder.
The 2013 molecular dynamics study of BTK PH domain mutants including R28C/H examined changes in the Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding site, implying R28 lies in the ligand site.
No experimental structure with R28H itself was found; the residue-28 structures are R28C (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK) or the wild-type reference.
payload.why_it_matters: A substitution-specific structure would show whether His at 28 changes the pocket or fold directly, rather than inferring from R28C.

payload.statement: R28H removes the basic arginine side chain that contacts the inositol phosphate head group in the PH-domain lipid pocket (UniProt binding site at 28), so the mutant PH domain loses PI(3,4,5)P3/IP4-dependent membrane recruitment and BTK cannot be activated at the plasma membrane.
payload.would_refute: The ligand contact test finds that residue 28 is not a neighbour of the inositol phosphate (4IP) or any other ligand in the IP4-bound structures 1B55 and 1BWN, with distances well beyond contact range.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Residue 28 carries a UniProt experimental binding-site annotation for inositol tetrakisphosphate, 4IP-bound PH structures exist, and the 2013 MD study targeted this site; ClinVar pathogenicity and high AlphaMissense/conservation scores support a functional site.

payload.statement: R28H destabilises the BTK PH domain fold, so the mutant domain is partly unfolded or mis-packed and cannot support lipid binding or kinase activation, independent of any direct loss of ligand contact.
payload.would_refute: FoldX predicts a folding free-energy change in the neutral range (below the destabilising threshold of about 1 kcal/mol) on the AlphaFold model, and the same is true of the other pathogenic substitutions at residue 28.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: High conservation (0.962) and AlphaMissense (0.9978) suggest structural importance, but the residue is an exposed-looking arginine with no recorded stability measurement, so this ranks below the binding-site hypothesis.

payload.statement: R28H disrupts a protein-protein contact on the PH domain surface used for BTK partner binding (such as GTF2I or IBTK), so BTK loses assembly with a partner needed for signalling, rather than losing lipid binding.
payload.would_refute: The structural context test finds residue 28 outside every predicted protein-protein interface and outside any predicted pocket on the AlphaFold model.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProt records PH-domain-mediated binding to GTF2I and IBTK, but no source places residue 28 at those interfaces, so this is the least supported class.

payload.description: Check whether residue 28 neighbours an inositol phosphate or other ligand in the 39 experimental structures that observe it. Supports H1 if 4IP-bound structures list residue 28 as a neighbour; refutes H1 if not.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A contact with 4IP would strongly favour H1 and weaken H2 and H3; no contact would move H1 down sharply, since the test is directly about the ligand-binding hypothesis.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run true with 39 structures observing residue 28 and holding a non-solvent ligand; it costs 0 compute seconds and 2 tool calls, with no approval needed.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change of R28H on the AlphaFold model, with the same value for other substitutions at residue 28. Supports H2 if destabilising; weakens H2 if neutral.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value would raise H2, but it does not separate H1 from H3 and FoldX errors are near 1 kcal/mol.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Reported as ok via EBI ProtVar, 0 compute seconds, no approval needed.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Predicted pocket and protein-protein interface membership of residue 28 on the AlphaFold model. Supports H3 if in a predicted interface; weakly supports H1 if in a predicted pocket.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Predicted interface membership would move H3; predicted pocket membership would only weakly support H1, so it resolves less than the ligand contact test.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: ProtVar pocket data answers; interface state is not_covered, so the interface part may be unavailable; 0 compute seconds.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Reference versus R28H structure prediction on the 1-143 construct using ESM Atlas, with local and global RMSD and site pLDDT. Would weakly test H2 and H3.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Structure predictors are not validated for single substitutions, so a matching fold is uninformative and a change would be weak evidence.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Needs human approval and costs 120 compute seconds of the 300 budget; an existing result is cached, so the run is possible but expensive.
controls: Same provider, model version and construct for both sequences.
Residues with low confidence in either model are masked before the RMSD is computed.

payload.rationale: T1 (ligand contact) is the highest expected-learning test at zero compute cost, needs no approval, and directly tests the top-ranked hypothesis H1 against the binding-site annotation. It leaves the 300-second compute budget intact.

rejected.reason: Stability test is informative mainly for H2 and is lower expected learning (0.5); run later if H1 is not confirmed.
Structural context gives only weak support to H1 and its interface data is not_covered, so it resolves less.
Requires human approval, costs 120 of 300 compute seconds, and structure predictors are not validated for single substitutions, so the expected learning is low (0.3).

payload.findings: review_claims checked 24 statements: no clinical or treatment wording, no evidence without a source, all 3 hypotheses labelled as agent-generated. T1 is retrieval only, requires no approval, and starts no job.

payload.summary: Residue 28 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures that observe it. The inositol phosphate 4IP contacts it in 4 of 6 instances (minimum 2.75 Å, in 1B55 and 1BWN), and the closest contact is 2.58 Å to 4PT in 2Z0P. The negative-control ions ZN and MG never neighbour the residue, and the four R28C-mutated structures show 0 ligand contacts.

Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.

limitations: A crystal contact with a soluble analogue is not a measurement of binding by the variant protein.
Absence of a ligand-bound structure is not evidence of absence of binding.

per_hypothesis.why: Residue 28 is within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures, and 4IP contacts it at 2.75 Å minimum in 4 of 6 instances, so the residue sits in the inositol-phosphate site. Ion negative controls ZN and MG never neighbour it, which argues against a generic metal-proximity artefact.
A ligand contact says nothing about fold stability, so the test neither supports nor refutes the destabilisation hypothesis.
The test measures ligand contact, not protein-protein interface membership, so it does not bear on the partner-binding hypothesis.

payload.uncertainty: The measurement is contact with soluble ligands in crystal structures, not binding by the variant protein; the four R28C structures show no ligand contact, but they carry the mutation and do not directly test loss of contact by His. Ligand contact within 4.5 Å does not show that R28H abolishes binding or that loss of binding causes the loss of function, and no R28H structure exists in the record. Ligand-bound structures are dominated by a few compound series, so the 32 of 39 count reflects repeated entries.

payload.why: T1 measured that residue 28 is within 2.75 Å of 4IP in 4 of 6 instances and within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 structures, while ion controls never contact it [T1]. This is consistent with the UniProt inositol-phosphate binding annotation [E3, E4] and supports H1 as the favoured mechanism, with H2 and H3 unchanged in rank.

payload.description: Run the FoldX stability test (T2) on R28H and the other residue-28 substitutions to check whether the variant also destabilises the PH fold. Outcome that would confirm H1 over H2: a neutral predicted ddG (below about 1 kcal/mol), which leaves the loss of inositol-phosphate contact as the leading explanation. A destabilising value would instead raise H2 as a co-mechanism.
payload.why_now: The ligand contact result favours H1, but H2 has not been tested, and separating the two needs a stability measurement before any structure comparison spends the 120-second compute budget.

## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains loss of function of BTK p.Arg28His (UniProt Q06187, residue 28), and which single computational test discriminates between the candidates? These are agent-generated hypotheses for research only.

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies NM_000061.3 c.83G>A (p.Arg28His) as Pathogenic with no conflicts [E1]. UniProtKB lists the variant as a moderate X-linked agammaglobulinemia variant [E2]. UniProtKB annotates residue 28 as an experimental binding site for inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate within the PH domain, residues 3-133 [E3, E4]. AlphaMissense scores the substitution 0.9978 [E5], and ScoreCons gives residue 28 a conservation of 0.962 [E6]. A 2013 molecular dynamics study examined the inositol-phosphate site in R28C/H mutants [E10]. No measured stability value or R28H-specific structure was found [G1, G2].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (ligand binding, starting rank 1): the arginine side chain contacts the inositol phosphate head group, so R28H loses lipid-dependent membrane recruitment [H1].
H2 (stability, rank 2): R28H destabilises the PH fold [H2].
H3 (protein interaction, rank 3): R28H disrupts a PH-domain surface used for partner binding [H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
Four tests were available: ligand contact, stability, structural context, and reference-versus-variant structure prediction, which needs approval and 120 compute seconds [T1, T2, T3, T4]. The ligand contact test was chosen because it has the highest expected learning, needs no approval and costs no compute time [T1].

## Result
Residue 28 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures [T1]. The inositol phosphate 4IP contacts it at a minimum of 2.75 Å in 4 of 6 instances [T1]. The ion controls ZN and MG never neighbour residue 28 [T1]. The four R28C-mutated structures show no ligand contact [T1].

## Updated decision
H1 remains favoured because the measured contact supports it [T1, H1]. H2 and H3 are unchanged, since the ligand test measures neither stability nor interfaces [T1]. The favoured hypothesis did not change [decision].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The contact test uses crystal structures with soluble ligands, not binding by the variant protein [T1]. The R28C structures carry a different substitution, and no R28H structure exists in the record [G2]. Loss of contact has not been shown to cause loss of function. Validation still needed: a stability measurement to exclude H2, and binding measurements of R28H against inositol phosphate.

## Next experiment
Run the FoldX stability test on R28H and the other residue-28 substitutions [T2]. A neutral predicted change would leave H1 leading; a destabilising value would raise H2 as a co-mechanism.
